items.label: DOLCE+DnS Ultralite

items.label: SKOS

items.label: PROTON Top

items.label: PROTON Ext

items.label: Situation ODP

items.label: Sequence ODP

items.label: Time-indexed situation ODP

items.label: Time interval ODP

items.label: Participation ODP

items.label: Information Realisation ODP

items.label: IRW Web Resource ODP
items.description: Ontology describing identification of web resources through URI/HTTP relationships and representations.

items.label: Object-with-states ODP
items.description: Content ODP for modelling objects that have discrete states over time.

items.label: isCharacterisedBy ODP
items.description: ODP for characterising a subject by assigning qualifiable or quantifiable attributes.

items.label: IOLite
items.description: Ontology of information objects, encodings, and realisations as a plugin to DOLCE-Ultralite.

items.label: Entity with Provenance ODP
items.description: Core ODP of PROV

items.label: Part-whole ODP
items.description: ODP for part-whole relations, including transitive and intransitive part-of properties and parthood types.

items.label: Description ODP
items.description: ODP for Description, related to DnS.

items.label: Descriptions and Situations
items.description: ODP for the Description and Situation (DnS) pattern, connecting descriptions to the situations they describe.

items.label: Born Digital Archive ODP
items.description: ODP for Born Digital Archives.

items.label: Social Relation ODP
items.description: ODP for social relationships between agents, including temporal indexing and role-based characterisation.

items.label: FOAF

items.label: W3C Org

items.label: Person Core

items.label: Bio vocabulary

items.label: Participation schema

items.label: Whois vocabulary

items.label: Meetups Ontology

items.label: Geonames

items.label: Timeline

items.label: SEAS Time

items.label: TempO bitemporal

items.label: Historical Territory

items.label: Geologic Timescale

items.label: Places vocabulary

items.label: ATM temporal/spatial

items.label: Building Topology (BOT)

items.label: GLEIF Geocoding

items.label: BIBO

items.label: FaBiO

items.label: DoCO

items.label: BiRO

items.label: CiTO

items.label: CiTO Functions

items.label: BIBFRAME

items.label: MADS/RDF

items.label: ISBD

items.label: RDA Expression

items.label: RDA Group 1

items.label: RDA Group 2

items.label: RDA Group 3
items.description: RDA elements for preferred and variant names for concepts, places, and events.

items.label: RDA Manifestation
items.description: RDA element set for attributes and relationships of the Manifestation entity.

items.label: RDA WEMI Relationships

items.label: RDA GR2 Relationships

items.label: RDA Work

items.label: PRO Publishing Roles

items.label: PSO Publication Status

items.label: PWO Publication Workflow

items.label: R4R Resource Reuse

items.label: Research Artifacts
items.description: Informatics Research Artifacts Ontology for describing research outputs using OWL and RDF Schema.

items.label: CIDOC-CRM
items.description: ISO 21127 reference ontology for the exchange and integration of cultural heritage information.

items.label: Erlangen CRM
items.description: OWL DL implementation of CIDOC-CRM developed at Friedrich-Alexander-University Erlangen-Nuremberg.

items.label: CRMinf Argumentation
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for modelling argumentation, inference making, belief adoption, propositions, and interpretative reasoning.

items.label: CRMsci Scientific Observation
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for scientific observations, measurements, empirical assessment, hypothesis formation, and interpretation of evidence.

items.label: CRMgeo Spatiotemporal
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension integrating geospatial and temporal reasoning with GeoSPARQL and GIS-compatible representations.

items.label: CRMarchaeo Archaeology
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for archaeological excavations, stratigraphy, finds processing, and archaeological documentation workflows.

items.label: CRMdig Digital Provenance
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for digitisation processes, digital provenance, computational derivation, and production metadata.

items.label: CRMtex Textual Entities
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for manuscripts, inscriptions, textual carriers, writing systems, and textual interpretation.

items.label: CRMba Built Archaeology
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension supporting archaeological analysis and documentation of standing buildings and architectural stratification.

items.label: CRMpe Phenomenology
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for modelling phenomenological relations in built heritage and spatial perception of monuments.

items.label: CRMsoc Social Phenomena
items.description: CIDOC CRM extension for modelling social relations, group dynamics, memberships, and social historical phenomena.

items.label: LRMoo
items.description: Object-oriented implementation of the IFLA Library Reference Model harmonised with CIDOC CRM for bibliographic and cultural heritage resources.

items.label: FRBRoo
items.description: CIDOC CRM harmonisation of the FRBR bibliographic model for works, expressions, manifestations, and items.

items.label: PRESSoo
items.description: CIDOC CRM-compatible ontology for serials, continuing resources, and bibliographic publishing workflows.

items.label: SDHSS
items.description: Semantic Data for Humanities and Social Sciences ecosystem extending CIDOC CRM for interoperable humanities research data.

items.label: Erlangen CRM
items.description: OWL DL 1.0 implementation of CIDOC-CRM developed at Friedrich-Alexander-University Erlangen-Nuremberg.

items.label: Europeana Data Model
items.description: Integration medium for collecting, connecting and enriching descriptions provided by Europeana data providers.

items.label: ArCo (root)

items.label: ArCo network

items.label: ArCo Location

items.label: ArCo Context Description
items.description: ArCo module for contextual attributes of cultural properties: agents, objects, activities, and situations.

items.label: ArCo Cultural Event

items.label: ArCo Catalogue

items.label: ArCo Denotative Description
items.description: ArCo module encoding measurable characteristics of cultural properties: materials, techniques, measurements, conservation status.

items.label: Cultural Institutes/Sites
items.description: Ontology for data on cultural institutes or sites: agents, locations, contact points, multimedia, and events.

items.label: VIR Visual Iconography
items.description: OWL extension of CIDOC-CRM for visual elements and iconographic interpretation, supporting denotation and signification.

items.label: ICON Iconology
items.description: Ontology conceptualising Panofsky's levels of art interpretation: pre-iconographical, iconographical, iconological.

items.label: SeaLiT Maritime History
items.description: Formal ontology extending CIDOC-CRM v7.1.1 for integration of heterogeneous maritime history information sources.

items.label: CWRC Writing Research
items.description: Ontology of the Canadian Writing Research Collaboratory.

items.label: Shoah persecution domain
items.description: Beta ontology describing the persecution and deportation of Jews in Italy between 1943 and 1945.

items.label: PREMIS Preservation
items.description: Library of Congress ontology for preservation metadata describing intellectual entities, objects, events, agents, and rights.

items.label: LODE Historical Events
items.description: Ontology for publishing descriptions of historical events as Linked Data, with mappings to other event vocabularies.

items.label: SAWS Ancient Wisdoms
items.description: Ontology for the Sharing Ancient Wisdoms project, representing medieval Greek and Arabic wisdom literature.

items.label: INTRO Intertextuality
items.description: Ontology for intertextual, interpictorial, and intermedial relations in literary and art studies.

items.label: Linked Art Metadata Application Profile
items.description: CIDOC CRM-based metadata application profile for art museum data exchange. Streamlines the full CRM complexity to cover 90% of use cases for 90% of organizations with only 10% of its complexity.[reference:10] Focuses on three core entity types (Objects, Actors, and Events) and practical implementation patterns adopted by institutions including Getty, Smithsonian, and The Met.[reference:11][reference:12]

items.label: PROV-O
items.description: W3C PROV Ontology — family of documents supporting provenance interchange on the Web.

items.label: PAV
items.description: Lightweight ontology for tracking Provenance, Authoring, and Versioning of online resources, specialising PROV-O.

items.label: P-Plan
items.description: PROV-O extension for representing scientific plans (bundles of steps and variables) alongside execution records.

items.label: Dublin Core Elements

items.label: DC Terms

items.label: DC Type
items.description: DCMI Type Vocabulary — approved terms for the Resource Type element identifying the genre of a resource.

items.label: DC Abstract Model
items.description: Abstract model for Dublin Core metadata underlying the DCMI specifications.

items.label: SKOS
items.description: Simple Knowledge Organization System — common data model for sharing and linking KOS via the Semantic Web.

items.label: SKOS-XL
items.description: SKOS extension providing additional support for describing and linking lexical entities in concept schemes.

items.label: ISO 25964 SKOS-Thes
items.description: Vocabulary for interoperability between SKOS and ISO 25964-1:2011 (thesaurus standard).

items.label: UNESCO SKOS ext.

items.label: DCAT

items.label: MOD Ontology metadata
items.description: Metadata for Ontology Description and publication — describing ontologies themselves.

items.label: MDR DCAT profile
items.description: Application profile of DCAT combining VoID, DCTERMS, and LIME for the Semantic Turkey platform.

items.label: Schema.org
items.description: Shared vocabulary used by Bing, Google, Yahoo!, and Yandex to improve search result display.

items.label: DBpedia Ontology
items.description: Classes and properties used in the DBpedia dataset, extracted from Wikipedia infoboxes.

items.label: DataCite Ontology
items.description: OWL 2 DL ontology enabling DataCite Metadata Specification v2.0 properties to be described in RDF.

items.label: OAI-ORE aggregations
items.description: Open Archives Initiative ORE — standards for description and exchange of aggregations of web resources.

items.label: DAQ Data Quality
items.description: Vocabulary for allowing owners/users of RDF data to calculate quality metrics on multiple resource types.

items.label: MARC Relators
items.description: MARC relator terms defined as both RDF properties and SKOS concepts for bibliographic relationships.

items.label: OntoLex-Lemon core
items.description: W3C model for representing lexical information relative to ontologies. Core module.

items.label: Lemon (legacy)
items.description: Original Lemon lexicon model for ontologies — predecessor to OntoLex, covering morphology, syntax, and lexicon-ontology mapping.

items.label: GOLD
items.description: General Ontology for Linguistic Description — created for applications in descriptive linguistics.

items.label: LMM L2
items.description: Ontology for aligning existing linguistic ontologies and describing NLP research objects.

items.label: Semiotics ODP
items.description: ODP encoding a basic semiotic theory: Expression, Meaning, Reference, and LinguisticAct.

items.label: Semio vocabulary
items.description: Vocabulary to describe signs in a semiotic approach.

items.label: PreMOn FrameNet
items.description: PreMOn FrameNet module extending the core module for FrameNet-specific concepts.

items.label: PreMOn NomBank
items.description: PreMOn NomBank module extending the core module for NomBank predicate concepts.

items.label: PreMOn PropBank
items.description: PreMOn PropBank module extending the core module for PropBank-specific concepts.

items.label: PreMOn VerbNet
items.description: PreMOn VerbNet module with classes and properties specific to the VerbNet predicate model.

items.label: GND Authority File
items.description: Gemeinsame Normdatei (German Integrated Authority File) — broad element set for describing authorities.

items.label: FRAD Authority Data
items.description: IFLA Functional Requirements for Authority Data — element set of native RDF classes and properties.

items.label: MUTO Tagging
items.description: Modular and Unified Tagging Ontology — unified schema for common, semantic, group, private, and automatic tagging.

items.label: OnTopic thesaurus
items.description: Ontology of topics as used in thesauri and subject directories.

items.label: Web Annotation (OA)
items.description: W3C Open Annotation Core — interoperable framework for creating associations between resources.

items.label: FEL Entity Linking
items.description: RDF vocabulary for describing and categorising annotations involving entity mentions linked to knowledge base identifiers.

items.label: Biol taxonomy
items.description: RDF vocabulary for the taxonomy of all forms of life.

items.label: Event (C4DM)
items.description: C4DM ontology dealing with the notion of reified events seen as first-class objects.

items.label: Lifecycle Schema
items.description: Classes and properties specifying a lifecycle that any resource may pass through.

items.label: PKO Procedural Knowledge
items.description: Procedural Knowledge Ontology — models procedures, their executions, and related resources and agents.

items.label: CEON Process ODP
items.description: Core ODP of the CEON ontology network defining aspects of the process concept.

items.label: OntoMedia Being
items.description: Vocabulary to describe interactions between persons and groups occurring in multimedia.

items.label: OntoMedia Expression
items.description: OntoMedia core expression ontology for describing interactions in multimedia contexts.

items.label: Music Ontology
items.description: Main concepts and properties for describing music: artists, albums, tracks, performances on the Semantic Web.

items.label: DOREMUS Music
items.description: DOREMUS extension of FRBRoo for describing musical works and their performances.

items.label: Chord Ontology
items.description: First-draft chord ontology from QMUL Centre for Digital Music, providing vocabulary for chords and chord sequences.

items.label: Polifonia Ontology Network (PON)
items.description: The FULL module of the Polifonia Ontology Network (PON), a modular ontology network for representing tangible and intangible musical cultural heritage assets. This module imports all other PON modules to provide a comprehensive backbone. Aligned with DOREMUS, Music Ontology, MusicOWL, and Wikidata.[reference:0][reference:1]

items.label: PON Core
items.description: Core ontology module of the Polifonia Ontology Network. Models general-purpose concepts and ontology design patterns (place, time, classification, situation) that are reused across all other PON modules. Includes the Music Time Interval ODP for musical timing information.[reference:2]

items.label: PON Music Meta
items.description: Foundational module of PON for achieving interoperability of music metadata. Provides a rich ontology to describe artists, compositions, performances, recordings, and casts. Focuses on provenance and is based on the Information-Realisation ODP. Aligned with Music Ontology, DOREMUS, and Wikidata.[reference:3]

items.label: PON Music Representation
items.description: Foundational module of PON to describe arbitrary musical content (scores, audio tracks). Provides a schema for describing music analysis based on theoretical interpretations. Represents annotations of musical object fragments (notes, chords) with temporal locations.[reference:4]

items.label: PON Music Instrument
items.description: Foundational module of PON for representing musical instruments and their evolution through time and space. Models instruments as cultural objects with historical and geographical dimensions.[reference:5]

items.label: PON Source
items.description: Foundational module of PON for representing music-related sources (manuscripts, articles, interviews, reviews). Provides support for describing source creators, types, production context, usage, and multimedia documents (score images, audio, video).[reference:6]

items.label: PON Music Annotation
items.description: Module providing a comprehensive framework for music annotations of different types and syntaxes. Includes the JAMS Ontology (JSON Annotated Music Specification) for reproducible MIR research. Enhances interoperability between music annotation formats.[reference:7]

items.label: PON Tunes
items.description: Specialisation of the Music Meta module for folk music representation. Extends Music Meta to address specific requirements of folk music traditions and repertoires.[reference:8]

items.label: PON CoMeta
items.description: Extension of the Music Meta module to represent music corpora. Supports the description and management of large-scale music collections and datasets.[reference:9]

items.label: PON Music Projection
items.description: Module for achieving interoperability of music notation systems. Provides a model for representing different musical notations and their relationships.[reference:10]

items.label: PON Music Analysis
items.description: Module for music analysis through reasoning using modal-tonal theories. Supports computational analysis and reasoning about musical structures and relationships.[reference:11]

items.label: PON Music Algorithm
items.description: Module for describing computational methods for music and their parameterization. Enables representation and reproducibility of music processing algorithms.[reference:12]

items.label: PON Organs
items.description: Rich descriptive model of musical organs and building methods. Represents organ specifications, construction techniques, and historical organ data.[reference:13]

items.label: PON Bells
items.description: Ontology for describing bells, bell towers, and bell ringers. Represents measurable aspects of bells (weight), authorship attribution, and relationships to bell towers and ringers.[reference:14][reference:15]

items.label: PON MEETUPS
items.description: Ontology representing concepts and relationships describing encounters between people in the musical world in Europe from c. 1800 to c. 1945. Models participants, places, event types, reasons (music making, personal life, business), and dates of historical musical meetups.[reference:16][reference:17]

items.label: PON Roman Chord
items.description: Ontology for representing Roman chord notations in music analysis. Provides vocabulary for chord descriptions and relationships to musical objects.[reference:18]

items.label: EmOCA Emotion
items.description: EmOCA — contextualises dimensional emotion and categorises it for human readability.

items.label: Cognitive Characteristics
items.description: Cognitive Characteristics Ontology — vocabulary for describing cognitive patterns, their temporal dynamics, and origins.

items.label: BDI Agent Architecture
items.description: Formal framework modelling the Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) architecture for rational agents.

items.label: Digital Twin
items.description: Digital Twin ontology defining Digital Twins, Semantic Digital Twins, and aggregations using Web of Things.

items.label: Digital Ecosystem Model Ontology
items.description: The DEM is an ontology that uses the Web Ontology Language (OWL). A DEM supports the analysis and management of a Digital Ecosystem. A Digital Ecosystem (DE) should be interpreted as a concept with the purpose for analysing and modelling the ability of infrastructure to maintain the usefulness of digital objects. A digital ecosystem consists of a set of the entities and dependencies influencing or necessary for a successful use at a later point in time.

items.label: Heritage Digital Twin Ontology
items.description: A novel ontology for cultural heritage based on the concept of digital twin. The ontology, called Heritage Digital Twin ontology, is a compatible extension of the well-known CIDOC CRM ISO standard for cultural heritage documentation and incorporates all the different documentation systems presently in use for cultural heritage documentation.

items.label: OGDL4M
items.description: Ontology of Open Government Data Licenses Framework for a Mash-up Model (OGDL4M), version 0.1 Please visit Wiki section for further information.

items.label: Cultural Artefact Contextual Ontology
items.description: The CACAO ontology was developed in collaboration with four CH institutes, validating its applicability and understandability across diverse data types. The ontology extends CIDOC-CRM by integrating ODRL for structured rights expression and by introducing new, more specific concepts for detailed contextual information.

items.label: Creative Commons REL
items.description: CC Rights Expression Language for describing copyright licenses in RDF.

items.label: OeGov CC Ontology
items.description: Creative Commons ontology extending the CC RDF schema for the OeGov context.

items.label: ODRL Rights Language
items.description: Open Digital Rights Language — flexible, interoperable mechanisms for digital content rights in publishing and distribution.

items.label: Open Data Rights
items.description: ODI vocabulary supporting machine-readable rights statements for open data publication.

items.label: Copyright Ontology
items.description: Ontology for copyright-aware Digital Rights Management (DRM) systems.

items.label: LiMo Licenses
items.description: Vocabulary for describing software and content licenses as linked data.

items.label: TRO Transparency Relations
items.description: Vocabulary representing transparency relations typically between powerful people or institutions.

items.label: GDPRov
items.description: OWL2 ontology for provenance metadata of consent and data lifecycles towards documenting GDPR compliance.

items.label: DPV Personal Data
items.description: Extension to the Data Privacy Vocabulary providing additional categories of personal data.

items.label: GLEIF Legal Entity
items.description: Ontology for Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) registration — Level 1 key reference data for legal entities.

items.label: JudO Judicial Interpretations
items.description: OWL ontology library modelling judicial interpretations, legal subsumption, interpretative acts, and legal reasoning processes.

items.label: LKIF Core
items.description: Legal Knowledge Interchange Format ontology including norms, argumentation, interpretations, legal roles, and reasoning structures.

items.label: GLEIF Parent relationships
items.description: Ontology for LEI parent relationships: direct and ultimate accounting consolidating parents.

items.label: GLEIF Base
items.description: Generic concepts reused by other GLEIF ontologies: legal entities, relationships, statuses, names, and addresses.

items.label: GLEIF Entity Legal Form
items.description: Ontology for Entity Legal Forms and their abbreviations by jurisdiction, based on ISO 20275.

items.label: GLEIF Registration Authority
items.description: Concepts for business registries including the jurisdictions they serve.

items.label: PICO Evidence Model
items.description: Machine-accessible PICO framework for describing evidence: Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome.

items.label: AIRO AI Risk (AI Act)
items.description: AI Risk Ontology representing AI risk concepts and relations based on the EU AI Act draft and ISO 31000.

items.label: NYON Legal concepts
items.description: Ontology representing concepts in the legal domain.

items.label: Timbus and related ontologies
items.description: A set of ontolgoies developed in the Timbus project for describing digital preservation, including the Timbus Preservation Ontology and related ontologies for describing digital objects, preservation actions, and preservation metadata.

items.label: Collections Ontology
items.description: CO defines unordered (Set, Bag) and ordered (List) collections, inspired by Drummond et al.'s OWL sequences work.

items.label: Argument Model Ontology
items.description: Ontology implementing structured argumentation patterns including claims, warrants, rebuttals, evidence, and supports.

items.label: Argument Interchange Format
items.description: Ontology for representing argument structures, inference nodes, conflicts, premises, and conclusions in computational argumentation.

items.label: HiCO Historical Context
items.description: Ontology for representing the hermeneutical context of interpretative acts, including criteria, motivations, and source attributions.

items.label: Observable Properties
items.description: General-purpose ontology for observable properties supporting qualitative and quantitative descriptions.

items.label: SALT Annotation
items.description: Ontology connecting rhetorical and argumentative structures with textual fragments and scholarly discourse.

items.label: Marl Opinion/Sentiment
items.description: Schema for modelling subjective opinions, sentiment polarity, and evaluative judgements expressed by agents.

items.label: MUNC Uncertainty
items.description: OWL vocabulary for describing uncertainty metadata about RDF statements.

items.label: ORCA Certainty/Attribution
items.description: Ontology of Reasoning, Certainty and Attribution for characterising how information is known and its source.

items.label: RiC-O Records in Contexts
items.description: ICA OWL 2 ontology for describing archival record resources — formal representation of the RiC Conceptual Model (RiC-CM). Version 1.1 released May 2025.

items.label: EAC-CPF Archival Agents
items.description: OWL ontology derived from the EAC-CPF XML schema (IBC Emilia-Romagna / Regesta.exe) for encoding names and contexts of creators of archival materials.

items.label: OAD Archival Description
items.description: Ontology of Archival Description (2012, ReLOAD project / Archivio Centrale dello Stato, IBC, Regesta.exe) — OWL model covering common archival metadata elements, integrated with an ISAD(G) SKOS ontology.

items.label: OCSA Cultural Organisations
items.description: Ontology of Cultural Organizations' Services and Access (2013, ReLOAD project) — describes services, facilities, and activities of institutions acting as archival holders.

items.label: SAN Archival
items.description: Ontology for the Italian National Archive System (SAN) linked data portal, covering fonds, archival institutions, and their relationships.

items.label: ArchOnto (EPISA)
items.description: CIDOC-CRM-based linked data model for archives developed in the Portuguese EPISA project (INESCTEC / Portuguese National Archives, Torre do Tombo). Modular: extends CRM with archival entities (ARE) and properties (ARP), plus an ISAD Ontology module.

items.label: ARKIVO archival collections
items.description: OWL 2 ontology (43 classes, 24 object properties) modelling archival description of historical document collections, developed for the Józef Piłsudski Institute of America collection.

items.label: P-Plan (archival plans)
items.description: PROV-O extension for representing plans and their execution, applicable to archival workflows such as appraisal, ingest, and description processes.

name: Multimedia Digital Object Representation in RDF

items.label: SCOTCH (3D Visualization)
items.description: Semantic Collaborative Ontology for Three-dimensional visualization of Cultural Heritage. Designed to document 3D visualizations, connecting parts of a 3D model internally and linking them to external data about physical remains [citation:6].

items.label: CHAD-AP (Acquisition & Digitization)
items.description: Cultural Heritage Acquisition and Digitization Application Profile. OWL ontology based on CIDOC-CRM, LRMoo, and CRMdig. Places digitization events (including 3D capture) and paradata at the core of the model. Used for the Ulisse Aldrovandi digital twin [citation:8].

items.label: HarvANA (3D Annotations)
items.description: System and RDF model for harvesting community annotations (tags) on 3D museum artefacts. Uses an ontology-directed folksonomy to represent user-generated content linked to specific 3D objects, enhancing discovery [citation:7].

items.label: 3D Point Cloud Segmentation
items.description: Semantic segmentation workflow for 3D point clouds (applied to San Giovanni a Porta Latina, Rome). Converts spatial classifications (constructive elements, materials, decay) into RDF/SPARQL-queryable formats for digital twins [citation:3].

items.label: OA Entry Ontology
items.description: OWL ontology developed for the Zeri Photo Archive project (University of Bologna). Models the Italian Scheda OA (Work of Art Entry) standard, capturing detailed descriptions of artworks including their physical characteristics, iconography, and state of preservation. Complements CIDOC-CRM for fine-grained art documentation [citation:2][citation:5].

items.label: F Entry Ontology (Photography)
items.description: OWL ontology developed alongside OA Entry for the Zeri Photo Archive. Models the Italian Scheda F (Photography Entry) standard, designed specifically for describing photographs as cultural heritage objects—including technical parameters (negative type, printing process), physical condition, and the relationship between photographic reproductions and their source artworks [citation:2][citation:7][citation:10].

items.label: ICONCLASS
items.description: Multilingual SKOS-based linked data service and de facto global standard for the subject classification of cultural heritage content, used for the description and retrieval of subjects in images and art.[reference:2][reference:3] Available as LOD in SKOS form since circa 2015 with over 1 million SKOS nodes across nine languages, retrievable by appending .rdf to a notation (e.g., http://iconclass.org/xyz.rdf).[reference:4][reference:5]

items.label: Art & Architecture Thesaurus (Getty)
items.description: Getty Vocabulary Program OWL ontology for the Art & Architecture Thesaurus (AAT). Defines 14 classes (gvp:Concept, gvp:Facet, gvp:GuideTerm, etc.) and 322 properties for describing concepts, hierarchies, and relationships in art and architecture terminology.[reference:6] Extends SKOS with domain-specific classes and relations; available under ODC-By 1.0 license.[reference:7]

items.label: Narrative Image Annotation Ontology
items.description: OWL ontology model for semantic annotation of narrative paintings and cultural heritage images. Combines Open Annotation Collaboration (OAC) framework with Plot as core element, mapping annotated regions to high-level semantics. Designed to represent plots and actions with appropriate granularity for temporal-spatial information modeling in cultural heritage.[reference:8] Supports annotation storage as RDF, CSV, and JSON via companion NIA tool.[reference:9]

items.label: IIIF Presentation API Ontology
items.description: RDF vocabulary for the International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF) Presentation API. Defines key classes for structuring digitized objects: Canvas (individual view/page), Manifest (complete object), Sequence (ordering of views), Range (structural hierarchy like chapters), Layer (grouping annotations), AnnotationList, and viewing hints (paged, continuous, facing-pages). IIIF Presentation 2.0+ APIs are designed as JSON-LD, making them native RDF ontologies for image-based cultural heritage resources [citation:3][citation:9].

items.label: Web Annotation Ontology (W3C)
items.description: W3C Recommendation for annotating web resources, including multimedia. Defines core classes: Annotation (container for annotation), Body (annotation content), Target (annotated resource), as well as specific selectors (FragmentSelector, CssSelector, XPathSelector) and motivation types (describing, commenting, tagging, identifying). Widely used for IIIF annotations and more broadly for image/audio/video fragment annotation [citation:1].

items.label: W3C Media Annotation Ontology (MA-ONT)
items.description: W3C Recommendation providing a core vocabulary for describing multimedia resources (audio, video, images) across formats. Defines properties covering: technical aspects (duration, frame size, encoding, bitrate, sample rate), content description (title, description, language), creation context (location, date, creator), publishing metadata (copyright, policy, target audience), and relationships between media resources. Harmonizes MPEG-7, EBUCore, Dublin Core, and other schemas [citation:2][citation:5].

items.label: EBUCore (Audiovisual Metadata)
items.description: EBU (European Broadcasting Union) ontology for describing audiovisual resources. Covers technical properties (format, codec, quality ratings), structural metadata (segments, parts, collections), and descriptive metadata (creator, genre, coverage). Extends MA-ONT and is aligned with schema.org. Includes EBUSport extension for sports media and CCDM for broadcast workflow integration. Particularly strong for born-digital video, broadcast archives, and time-based media [citation:5].

items.label: Lightweight Image Onto.
items.description: Lightweight Ontology for Describing Images.

items.label: VRA Core
items.description: VRA Core 4.0 — vocabulary for describing works of visual culture and their images.

items.label: Corago Semantic Model (Corago SM)
items.description: Linked Data and formal ontology for historical opera data (16th–20th century). Aligned with FRBRoo (FRBR object-oriented) and CIDOC-CRM to describe works, performances, librettos, and persons.

items.label: Drammar (Comprehensive Ontology of Drama)
items.description: OWL ontology (CC BY-ND 4.0) that describes and encodes core dramatic qualities as intangible cultural heritage, avoiding references to style and artistic qualities to represent cross-media dramatic elements. Uses a three-layered design (action, motivational, dramatic) mapped to characters' intentions and actions.

items.label: HYPERSTAGE Ontology
items.description: Under-development open knowledge base and ontology (PRIN 2022, University of Bologna) for semantic reconstruction of theatrical performances. Based on the 'Theatrical Performance' concept, designed to enable interoperability among decentralized Italian digital theatre archives and support immersive VR reconstructions.

items.label: Wikibase Theatre Production Model
items.description: Data model implemented in Wikibase for Linked Open Data representation of theatre productions, covering structural and scenographic aspects including costumes, spatial settings, and interactive audience elements. Enables complex SPARQL queries on productions, roles, and casts.

items.label: CapData Opéra Ontology
items.description: Opera houses ontology designed to define a common vocabulary and data interoperability for creative works and performances exchanged between opera houses. Aligned with schema.org and designed to promote interoperability.

items.label: SSHOC Performing Arts Model (SSHOCro)
items.description: CIDOC-CRM extension for performing arts data modeling, inheriting an event-centric orientation for representing performance-related information.
